scope: All 164 mapped parcels and all 69 recorded right holders reviewed at Tier 2 through the shared holder table. Free register records for every company holder, 180 selected free filings and independent and producer sources were screened. Twenty-two filings name 32 exact current references; no current farmer is verified.
rules: Recorded right holder, applicant, previous operator, authorised operator, verified operator and bottler are separate roles.
Only image-reviewed, explicitly assigned commune/reference rows become parcel events. Printed unresolved rows remain verbatim.
Unknown rights never suppress cadastral geometry. Current operation needs dated parcel-specific evidence under #364.
Domaine candidates come from the shared holder table; a company relation or recited lease is not farming evidence.
Tier 3 paid records and outreach remain deferred.

sources.title: DGFiP legal-entity parcel rights, 1 January 2025 (Côte-d’Or member)
sources.finding: Exact cadastral-reference rights only. All 69 recorded identifiers are inventoried, with every right code kept. A legal holder is a research contact, not a named operator or domaine.

sources.title: DGFiP yearly legal-entity parcel rights, 2019–2025
sources.finding: The bundle pins each departmental member’s hash and snapshot date. Seventy current parcels have a change; continuity requires the same SIREN. Provisional identifiers and names alone do not prove continuity.

sources.title: Cadastre Etalab parcel vintages, 2019–2026
sources.finding: Full, unsimplified Vougeot polygons and metric cru overlap. Every vintage is hash-pinned in the bundle. Sixteen current references pass the next-vintage and ≥95% containment rule; two later-generation candidates are rejected.

sources.title: Cerema DVF+ open-data, Bourgogne-Franche-Comté, April 2026 release
sources.finding: Twelve deeds name 22 current cru parcels. Commune records range from 26 March 2014 to 29 August 2025. Only dates, deed types and cadastral references/counts are retained; no prices, addresses or parties.

sources.title: Cadastre Etalab Vougeot lieux-dits, June 2026
sources.finding: CLOS DE VOUGEOT covers at least 99.99% of each selected parcel’s full geometry. Its exact polygon is clipped to INAO for the coverage audit; no historical subdivision or producer holding is converted into a cadastral alias.

sources.title: Bourgogne wine board: Clos de Vougeot official climat list
sources.finding: The appellation page lists one Grand Cru climat, Clos de Vougeot, and Vougeot as the producing commune. This corroborates the whole-cru name, not internal historical subdivisions.

sources.title: DGFiP release catalogue checked on 1 October 2026
sources.finding: The live official catalogue exposes the 2025 parcel attachment and no 2026 parcel attachment. The rights snapshot remains explicitly dated 1 January 2025.

sources.title: Partial authorisation: RC Les Grandes Vignes
sources.finding: Article 2 names four communes collectively. The fifteen rows are not assigned individually to communes; A469 is kept verbatim without a current parcel join. Article 1’s refusals concern Vosne-Romanée, not Vougeot.

sources.title: Repeated partial authorisation: RC Les Grandes Vignes

sources.title: Lambrays application receipt, dossier 2023-157

accessGaps: No parcel has verified operation evidence for 2026. Recited, mandated and executed leases are dated company evidence; actual operation, scope and continuation remain for #364.

Private individuals and other exclusions are absent from the DGFiP legal-entity dataset. Fifty-eight parcels without matched rights do not mean ownerless land; only A372 gained an exact-reference independent lead.

Free filing mirrors were screened by embedded text and OCR (RapidOCR on page images). OCR can miss handwritten or degraded references; a negative screen is limited to the selected filings, not every archive.

Three provisional identifiers (U18179935 GFA Dom Lamarche, U14149307 SCI Dom Leroy, U22314167 GFV Domaine Chantal Ropiteau) match a SIREN only by name and seat; no filing names their current references, so their links stay provisional or absent.
Ambiguous provisional identifiers (GFA Barrière, SA ASB, GFA Bachus 21, Maison Lejay-Lagoutte) remain unlinked; same-named companies are not assumed to be the recorded holder.

Producer holdings were obtained for three producers only; most estate sites render client-side or refused automated retrieval, and merchant pages for Grivot and Leroy returned 403/404. Their published areas are not compared.

The 2022 RC Les Grandes Vignes Article 2 table lists Flagey-Échezeaux, Vougeot, Comblanchien and Premeaux-Prissey collectively. It does not allocate its rows to communes. A469 is not attached to Vougeot A0469 from its matching number or area.
No outcome after the AF Gros, Lambrays or Eugénie application receipts is established. The 2026 Liger-Belair suspension is not authorisation or actual operation.

Regional coverage is 2019–September 2026; departmental coverage is 2016–2020. Five departmental alternate links remain unresolved in the shared archive. Negative screening results are limited to the indexed pages and OCR quality.

Historical internal names and producer holdings have no reviewed crosswalk to the pinned cadastral subdivisions. The whole-cru map remains the fallback; unresolved named-area/source work belongs to #344.
INAO and cadastre disagree at the edges. The source-bound 1084.3 m² reviewed cap records the measured remainder without adding a neighbouring commune or changing either geometry.
Paid land-registry (SPF) copies of the recited leases and domaine or CVI outreach are Tier 3 and were not used.

historyFindings.title: Sixteen current references with accepted lineage; two later-generation candidates rejected
historyFindings.finding: Seven retired references overlap the cru. Each accepted current successor first appears in the next vintage and lies at least 95% inside its retired predecessor. A0579/A0580 are rejected as direct successors to A0032 because they appear later; their accepted predecessor is A0562. Lineage is rule-based, not a division deed.

externalResearch.title: Domaine André Chopin, plot A372
externalResearch.finding: Winehog prints the plot number A372 and 0.3485 ha, exactly the cadastral area. It reports a 1980s purchase from the Prieur of Meursault, earlier farming by Chauvenet-Chopin and Domaine André Chopin’s first wine in 2019. The parcel has no company record.
externalResearch.appNote: Named by plot number (A372, 0.3485 ha, area matches): Domaine André Chopin’s plot from the 2019 vintage, per a 2020 article. Private ownership; current farming unconfirmed.

externalResearch.title: Gros Frère et Sœur, Musigni section plots
externalResearch.finding: Winehog lists plots 437, 438, 523, 524, 531, 532, 533 and 534 for Gros Frère et Sœur, 1.547 ha; their cadastral areas total 1.557 ha. None has a company record. From 2022 Domaine A.-F. Gros takes part in a swap; its 2022 application names A523 and A524 with Gros Frère et Sœur as previous operator.
externalResearch.appNote: Named by plot number in a 2020 article: Gros Frère et Sœur’s Musigni section (1.547 ha in eight plots), shared with Domaine A.-F. Gros from 2022. Private ownership; current farming unconfirmed.

externalResearch.title: Mugneret-Gibourg, plot 34
externalResearch.finding: Winehog names cadastre plot 34 (0.3424 ha, exactly the cadastral area), bought by Georges Mugneret in 1953. It is recorded to the société civile Domaine Georges Mugneret Gibourg.
externalResearch.appNote: Named by plot number (34, 0.3424 ha, area matches): bought by Georges Mugneret in 1953, per a 2020 article. Recorded to the domaine’s company; current farming unconfirmed.

externalResearch.title: Domaine Joseph Drouhin, Clos de Vougeot A40 (1940s lease)
externalResearch.finding: The original lease to the société civile du Domaine Joseph Drouhin, reproduced in a 1994 deed, names Vougeot section A no. 40, 62 ares, the current area of A40, for periods to 1951. The reference predates later cadastral revisions, and the parcel has no company record today. Historical lease only; current farming is not established.
externalResearch.appNote: Named in the 1940s lease to the Domaine Joseph Drouhin company (62 ares, matching today’s area), reproduced in a 1994 deed. Historical; the parcel has no company record and current farming is unconfirmed.

producerHoldings.finding: Independent 2016 article: largest owner with 5.48 ha. Compared with the GFV’s six parcels; no farming season stated.
Undated estate sheet: second-largest owner with about 2.5 ha. Compared with the MCPC and Clair Daü records; no parcels named.
Merchant text for the 2023 wine: a 2.21-ha parcel. Tenure not stated.
Estate page: 1.87 ha of vines in one continuous area. Tenure not stated.
Estate page: nearly 3 ha in one piece at the foot of the château. Compared with the Méo-Camuzet company records.
Estate page: 1 ha 26 a 69 ca in three parcels. Tenure not stated.
Merchant text for the 2020 wine: one 1.37-ha parcel on the upper slope; a 2022 article gives a single 1.36-ha parcel.
Importer page quoting critics: a 0.72-ha parcel against the southern wall (another review: three-quarters of a hectare).

parcelFilings.title: Château de la Tour: 1999 contribution

leaseEvidence.limitation: Ended on 11 November 2019 unless renewed; no renewal was found in the reviewed filings.

parcelFilings.finding: The 1999 contribution schedule, reproduced in statutes updated in 2003, names all six parcels; areas match the pinned cadastre. The recited 1993 métayage to Domaine Labet Déchelette ended on 11 November 2019; no later lease was found.
parcelFilings.appNote: 1999 contribution names this parcel (area matches). A 1993–2019 métayage of the vines to Domaine Labet Déchelette is recited; its 2026 object says the GFV now vinifies. No current parcel lease or season confirmed.

parcelFilings.title: GFA Misset Chéron: 2020 contribution and lease mandate

tenants: Domaine Misset Chéron (now Domaine du Couvent)
leaseEvidence.limitation: A mandate to sign, not an executed lease.

parcelFilings.finding: The founding statutes contribute A66 (1 ha 45 a 86 ca), free of any lease, and mandate a 24-year rural lease to the société civile then named Domaine Misset Chéron (443879218, now Domaine du Couvent). The executed lease was not reviewed.
parcelFilings.appNote: 2020 founding statutes contribute this parcel (area matches) and mandate a 24-year lease to Domaine Misset Chéron, now Domaine du Couvent. The signed lease and current farming are unverified.

parcelFilings.title: Les Héritiers Confuron: 2024 contribution and lease

leaseEvidence.limitation: The lease is recited and was delivered to the GFV; its text was not reviewed.

parcelFilings.finding: The 27 September 2024 founding deed contributes A393 and A406 (areas match), subject to a 24-year rural lease signed earlier that day to the SCE du Domaine Jean-Jacques Confuron (348024712). The deed matches the provisional rights identifier to SIREN 934003641.
parcelFilings.appNote: 2024 deed contributes this parcel (area matches), subject to a 24-year lease signed that day to the SCE du Domaine Jean-Jacques Confuron. Actual operation is not stated.

parcelFilings.title: GFA du Clos de(s) V: A511 and its rural lease

tenants: GAEC Coquard-Loison-Fleurot, now Domaine Coquard Loison Fleurot
leaseEvidence.limitation: Renewal recited in a later deed; the renewal itself was not reviewed.

parcelFilings.finding: A 2022 deed states the GFA’s only Vougeot property, A511 (22 a 10 ca, area matches), and recites its lease to Coquard-Loison-Fleurot (324549716), renewed on 16 October 2019 to 30 September 2037.
parcelFilings.appNote: A 2022 deed names this parcel (area matches) and recites its lease to Coquard-Loison-Fleurot, renewed 16 October 2019 to 2037. The renewal deed was not reviewed; actual operation unconfirmed.

parcelFilings.title: Domaine Jacques Prieur: property list
parcelFilings.finding: The 2013 statutes of Domaine Jacques Prieur list A45 and A384 with matching areas, crosswalking the provisional rights identifier to SIREN 778233098.
parcelFilings.appNote: Listed among Domaine Jacques Prieur’s properties in its 2013 statutes (area matches). Ownership context only; current farming unconfirmed.

parcelFilings.title: GFV Hudelot-Noëllat: acquisitions and contribution
parcelFilings.finding: The 2012 deed recites the 2005 contribution of A408 and the 2007 acquisition of A410 (areas match). Its 2002 acquisition of A409 reaches today’s A567 and A568 only through cadastral lineage. Leases are recited without tenants.
parcelFilings.appNote: Named in the GFV’s 2012 deed (area matches): acquired or contributed in 2005–2007. Its long-term leases are recited without tenants; current farming unconfirmed.

parcelFilings.title: GFV Hudelot-Noëllat: 2021 contribution
parcelFilings.finding: The 12 November 2021 contribution names A569 and A570 (areas match), both from the division of A407.
parcelFilings.appNote: Contributed to the GFV on 12 November 2021 (area matches), from the division of A407. Current farming unconfirmed.

parcelFilings.title: Drouhin-Laroze: 1995 transformation
parcelFilings.finding: The 7 June 1995 deed names A436 (59 a 92 ca, area matches, from A19). It also names A329, divided in November 1995 into A440 and A441; only A441 is now recorded to this company.
parcelFilings.appNote: Named in the 1995 deed transforming Drouhin-Laroze into a GFA (area matches). No lease reviewed; current farming unconfirmed.

parcelFilings.title: GFA du Domaine Méo Camuzet: A548 withdrawn
parcelFilings.finding: The 29 December 2016 deed withdraws A548 (area matches) from the GFA to its partners. Today A548 carries building-lease rights for this GFA and GFA Méo Camuzet Parents.
parcelFilings.appNote: Withdrawn from the Méo-Camuzet GFA to its partners on 29 December 2016 (area matches). Today’s rights are a building lease; current farming unconfirmed.

parcelFilings.title: GFV Saint-Vincent du Clos de Vougeot: founding contribution

tenants: an individual vigneron named in the deed
leaseEvidence.limitation: Published lease recited in a 2018 deed, which also records the tenant’s death; succession to the lease is not established.

parcelFilings.finding: The founding statutes contribute A517 (43 a 02 ca, area matches), bought that day from Domaine Prieuré Roch. A 2018 deed recites a published long-term lease of it, signed the same day, to an individual vigneron until 11 November 2032, and records the tenant’s death. No domaine is linked to the tenant.
parcelFilings.appNote: Contributed in 2006 (area matches) and let the same day under a published long-term lease to an individual vigneron, to 2032; a 2018 deed records the tenant’s death. Succession to the lease and current farming are unconfirmed.

parcelFilings.title: Les Vendanges du Clos: 1997 purchase and lease mandates

tenants: an individual vigneron named in the deed
leaseEvidence.limitation: A mandate in the founding statutes; the lease and its renewal were not reviewed.

parcelFilings.finding: The founding statutes mandate the purchase from the SAFER of A55 and A401, together 3,057 m² (matching the cadastre), and an 18-year lease from the 1997 harvest to an individual vigneron, paid in bottles. Execution and current farming are not established.
parcelFilings.appNote: The 1997 founding statutes mandate the purchase of A55 and A401 (3,057 m² together) and an 18-year lease to an individual vigneron. Mandates, not executed acts; current farming unconfirmed.

parcelFilings.title: GFV Saint-Vincent du Clos de Cîteaux: founding contribution

tenants: an individual vigneron named in the deed
leaseEvidence.limitation: Published lease recited in a 2011 deed; its continuation and current farming are not established.

parcelFilings.finding: The 2005 founding statutes contribute A516 (area matches), bought that day from SCEA Chanperdrix. The deed prints the commune as Vosne-Romanée, but the lieu-dit Le Clos de Vougeot, the appellation, the number and the area identify Vougeot A516. A 2011 deed recites its published long-term lease from 25 February 2005 to an individual vigneron.
parcelFilings.appNote: Contributed at the GFV’s 2005 foundation (area matches) and let from the same day under a published long-term lease to an individual vigneron, per a 2011 deed. Current farming unconfirmed.

parcelFilings.title: GFA Méo Camuzet Parents: contribution and lease mandate

leaseEvidence.limitation: A mandate in the founding deed; the 2025 rights file shows building-lease codes instead.

parcelFilings.finding: The 2016 founding deed contributes A548 (area matches), crosswalking the provisional identifier to SIREN 827608506, and mandates an 18-year rural lease to the GFA du Domaine Méo Camuzet. The 2025 rights file records a building lease between the two.
parcelFilings.appNote: Contributed in 2016 (area matches) with a mandate to lease it for 18 years to the Méo-Camuzet GFA. Today’s rights record a building lease between them; current farming unconfirmed.

parcelFilings.title: Fanabuca: 2015 purchase mandate
parcelFilings.finding: The founding statutes mandate the purchase of A461 and A462 (areas match) from private owners, on condition the vines are free of any lease. Both are now recorded to Fanabuca; no tenant is named.
parcelFilings.appNote: Named in Fanabuca’s 2015 purchase mandate (area matches), bought free of any lease. No tenant or producing domaine named; current farming unconfirmed.

parcelFilings.title: GFA Saint Martin: 2020 contribution and lease mandate

tenants: Domaine Misset Chéron (now Domaine du Couvent)
leaseEvidence.limitation: A mandate to sign, not an executed lease.

parcelFilings.finding: The 2020 founding statutes contribute A54 (60 a 40 ca, area matches), attributed that day from Domaine Misset Chéron’s capital reduction, and mandate a 24-year rural lease back to that company (443879218, now Domaine du Couvent). The signed lease was not reviewed.
parcelFilings.appNote: 2020 founding statutes contribute this parcel (area matches) and mandate a 24-year lease to Domaine Misset Chéron, now Domaine du Couvent. The signed lease and current farming are unverified.

parcelFilings.title: GFA de Châteauneuf: contribution and recited métayage

leaseEvidence.limitation: Recited in 2012 statutes; the 1959 private lease and any renewal were not reviewed.

parcelFilings.finding: The 2012 founding statutes contribute A272 (16 a 09 ca, area matches) and recite its métayage lease to Domaine Leroy under a private deed of 27 July 1959. The lease text and current operation were not reviewed.
parcelFilings.appNote: 2012 founding statutes name this parcel (area matches) and recite its métayage to Domaine Leroy under a 1959 private deed. The lease itself and current farming are unverified.

parcelFilings.title: GFA du Domaine Tortochot: A280 and its long lease

tenants: SCE du Domaine Tortochot, now SARL Domaine Tortochot
leaseEvidence.limitation: Executed and published lease recited in a 1997 deed; covers all GFA property. Its text was not reviewed.

parcelFilings.finding: The 1997 deed names A280 (21 a 33 ca, area matches) among the GFA’s property and recites the published 50-year lease of all that property, from 1 March 1986, to the SCE du Domaine Tortochot, now SARL Domaine Tortochot (337575906).
parcelFilings.appNote: Named in the GFA’s 1997 deed (area matches). All GFA land is let for 50 years from 1986 to the Tortochot operating company under a published lease; actual current operation is not stated.

parcelFilings.title: Famille Jean Dufouleur: 2015 contribution
parcelFilings.finding: The 2015 founding statutes contribute A3 (20 a 85 ca, area matches) free of any lease. The lease to Comptoir des Grands Vins recited in the same filing concerns a Nuits-Saint-Georges parcel, not this one.
parcelFilings.appNote: Contributed to the family GFA in 2015 (area matches), free of any lease. No lease or farming company is named for this parcel; current farming unconfirmed.

parcelFilings.title: GFA de la Grenelle: 1995 contribution of A433

tenants: an individual partner named in the deed
leaseEvidence.limitation: Published lease recited in the founding statutes; the tenant could bring it into a farming company. Any renewal was not reviewed.

parcelFilings.finding: The 1995 founding statutes contribute A433 (42 a 85 ca, area matches), already let for 18 years from 28 December 1994 to an individual partner. A 2004 deed states that all GFA land is let long-term to SCEV Château Genot-Boulanger; it names no reference.
parcelFilings.appNote: Contributed in 1995 (area matches) under an 18-year lease to an individual that ended in 2012. A 2004 deed says all GFA land is let to Château Genot-Boulanger; current farming unconfirmed.

parcelFilings.title: GFV Raphet: 2011 contribution of A412
parcelFilings.finding: The founding statutes contribute A412 (17 a 01 ca, area matches), acquired by exchange in 1990. The GFV may not farm directly and must let its land long-term; no lease or tenant is named.
parcelFilings.appNote: Contributed to the family GFV in 2011 (area matches). Its land must be let long-term, but no lease or tenant is named; current farming unconfirmed.

parcelFilings.title: GFA Domaine Xavier Liger-Belair: A75 in its statutes

leaseEvidence.limitation: The statutes say all contributed land is under long-term métayage leases; no tenant, date or parcel split is named.

parcelFilings.finding: The statutes updated in 2019 list the original contribution of A75 (72 a 45 ca, area matches) and state that all contributed land is let under long-term métayage leases. No tenant is named.
parcelFilings.appNote: Listed in the family GFA’s statutes, updated in 2019 (area matches). Its land is under long-term métayage leases whose tenants are not named; current farming unconfirmed.

parcelFilings.title: Domaine du Château de Marsannay: 1998 authorisation naming A264
parcelFilings.finding: A 1998 extraordinary meeting authorised contributing A264 (21 a 40 ca, area matches) and other vines to the Société Civile Coribel. The current rights file still records this company, so no transfer of A264 is shown. No lease is named.
parcelFilings.appNote: Named in the holder’s 1998 authorisation to contribute vines to another company (area matches); the rights file still records the holder. No lease named; current farming unconfirmed.

noticeReview.finding: Article 2 names four communes collectively. The fifteen rows are not assigned individually to communes; A469 is kept verbatim without a current parcel join. Article 1’s refusals concern Vosne-Romanée, not Vougeot.
The page names Vougeot A523 and A524, and Flagey D181 and D775 separately. The receipt does not authorise cultivation; its completion-date field is blank.
The same 4 July decision and Article 2 table reappear with a different published act ID. Retained as a second source occurrence, not a second independent parcel event.
The page names Vougeot A37, 0.3129 ha, and previous operator GUYON Jean Pierre. Application complete 21 August 2023; receipt alone does not authorise cultivation.
The annex names Vougeot A440. Application complete 25 October 2024 for 0.2294 ha; previous operator MAISON BOUCHARD PERE ET FILS. No later outcome is established.
Authorises a company-control operation under L.333-3 at constant land perimeter; Vougeot is mentioned, but no cadastral reference is given. Kept as context only, never an exact parcel authorisation.

The table explicitly assigns A1, A30 and A31 to Vougeot. Instruction is suspended for eight months from publication. Application registered 11 December 2025 and complete 6 January 2026; this is not an authorisation.
